bullets.title: July CPI in-line; Fed September hike odds slide to 36–45%
bullets.body: July headline CPI came in at +3.4% YoY / +0.1% MoM and core at +2.5% YoY / +0.2% MoM, all four reads matching consensus. Goldman Sachs and Baird called the print 'encouraging' and supportive of a September hold; CME futures priced September hike odds at 36% post-release while traders maintain ~45% per some feeds. Core goods rose 0.20% MoM (largest since Sept 2025), and median CPI dropped to a five-year low of 2.69% YoY.

bullets.title: NBIS blowout earnings: +454% YoY revenue, stock up 16%+
bullets.body: Nebius Group reported Q2 revenue of $582.3M (+454% YoY, +46% QoQ) vs. $557M consensus, with adjusted EBITDA of $236.2M vs. $158M expected (~50% AI Cloud margin). 2026 revenue guidance of $3.0–$3.4B and EoY ARR of $7–$9B were reiterated. Stock surged 16%+ on the day, though Michael Burry has reportedly called NBIS shorting 'shooting fish in a barrel.'

bullets.title: CRWV surges 20%+ post-earnings on doubled revenue; short interest was elevated
bullets.body: CoreWeave stock surged +20.5% after doubling revenue YoY on AI computing demand. Short interest heading into the print was 60M shares (16% of float, up from 25M in October), setting up a meaningful squeeze. One bearish voice flagged CRWV's $100B+ backlog and 59% adj. EBITDA margins as strong but cited 'problematic underlying financing methods.'

bullets.title: LITE first $1B quarter; CIEN flagged as primary read-through beneficiary
bullets.body: Lumentum reported its first $1B revenue quarter (Q4 FY26: $1.006B, +24.5% QoQ, +109.3% YoY). CIEN was explicitly flagged by an analyst agent as the primary beneficiary of LITE's earnings call and outperformed all other optical networking names on the day. GF Securities added both AMD and LITE to its preferred list as the AI rebound is expected to continue.

bullets.title: NVDA outperforms SOX; whale NVDA calls up 50% in two days; Jensen Huang ranked #1 CEO
bullets.body: NVDA is beginning to outperform the SOX index again, with one fintwit account noting a whale doubled down on NVDA calls two days prior and is now up 50% ($1.5M gain). NVDA's market cap increased $100B+ intraday, now nearly $1T larger than any peer. Separately, Jensen Huang was ranked #1 CEO on Glassdoor's 2026 list; ~50% of NVDA employees worth $25M+.

bullets.title: Grok 4.6 launches on NVIDIA GB300; claimed 3x cheaper than Fable at comparable quality
bullets.body: SpaceXAI released Grok 4.6 via API at $2/M input and $6/M output tokens, now live in Cursor and Grok Build. Early user data shows Grok is ~3x cheaper than Fable on long-running tasks with comparable quality, and 20x cheaper than Deepseek at lower quality. Grok 4.6 runs on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 with NVLink, and one analyst (Jonas) framed the Grok bot as the first step toward an enterprise AI platform combining intelligence, real-time data, low-cost compute, and connectivity.

bullets.title: TSMC CoWoS yield hits 99%; ABF substrates and DRAM remain supply bottlenecks for AI chips
bullets.body: TSMC's CoWoS packaging yield has cleared 99%, but ABF substrates ($100M–$500M investment, 18–24 months lead) and DRAM (>$15B, 3-year build) remain the binding constraints for AI chip supply. Substrates are expected to clear before DRAM. TSMC called out the ABF shortage a week after AT&S reportedly committed to more capacity.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasury auction draws highest yield since 2007; foreign demand soft
bullets.body: The 10-year note auction cleared at 4.683% (highest since 2007), with a 0.1bp tail indicating adequate demand at the margin. However, the bid-cover ratio fell to 2.53 from 2.59, and indirect (foreign) bidder take slipped to 76.7% from 81.5%. One fintwit account labeled the outcome 'Regime Change' for rates. Lacy Hunt also reportedly turned bearish on bonds.

bullets.title: US federal budget deficit widens sharply to $432B vs $346B forecast
bullets.body: The US federal budget deficit came in at $432.3B for the period, roughly $86B wider than the $346B forecast and well above the prior month's $120B. The widening represents a material macro headwind for duration assets.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz: Iran closes it, Trump claims 'total control,' traffic near standstill
bullets.body: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz remains closed with no policy change, while Trump posted on Truth Social that the US has 'total control' and intends to keep it. Ground reality: only 14 vessels crossed on Tuesday vs. ~120 per day pre-war, per Kpler. US intelligence reportedly expects Iran-related oil supply disruptions to persist through end of 2027.

bullets.title: US crude inventories surge 17.4M barrels, largest weekly build since January 2023
bullets.body: EIA data showed US crude stockpiles rose 17.4M barrels vs. a consensus draw of 1.8M barrels, the largest weekly build since January 2023. Cushing rose 1.6M barrels. WTI dipped on the release. Analysts flagged that energy price relief in July (gasoline -2.9% MoM) may reverse in August as crude and refining margins climb.

bullets.title: AI credit market stratifies into 4 layers; hyperscalers hold ~$2T incremental debt capacity
bullets.body: A Goldman Sachs pod highlighted that AI infrastructure debt issuance is crowding out traditional IG market, with hyperscalers collectively holding ~$2T of incremental debt capacity while maintaining IG ratings. AI credit divides into 4 risk layers: Layer 1 (hyperscaler senior unsecured) primarily faces technical spread widening risk. Capex growth rate is decelerating as capacity catches up to demand, improving hyperscaler FCF.

bullets.title: Open-weight AI models shift value toward compute; META, NVDA, ARM seen as beneficiaries
bullets.body: Open-weight models structurally shift economic value from closed model APIs toward compute infrastructure and inference. META, NVDA, and ARM are each seen as medium-magnitude beneficiaries of this shift. NVDA is highlighted as the highest-conviction positive read-through with strong GB300 demand, early Vera Rubin engagement, and large prepaid contracts.

bullets.title: Server CPU market modeled to hit $220B by 2030; AMD and Arm taking share from Intel
bullets.body: One semiconductor analyst describes the server CPU market as approaching an S-curve inflection point with charts set to 'look VERY different' through next year. Intel is expected to regain some share, but AMD and Arm continue growing, with potential for a three-way market split. The total server CPU TAM is modeled at ~$220B by 2030.

bullets.title: GOOGL launches Pixel 11 lineup with $100 price hike citing 'severe memory crunch'
bullets.body: Google debuted the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold. Base model starts at $899 (+$100 YoY); foldable at $1,899. The price increase was explicitly attributed to a 'severe memory crunch.' Google also unveiled Pixel Tags at $29/$99 for 4-pack (launching Nov 11), Pixel Watch 5 at $399, and wearables with insulin resistance tracking—a category first.

bullets.title: Yardeni raises S&P 500 target to 8,400; fear/greed index at 62 (greed); VIX 7-month low
bullets.body: Ed Yardeni raised his S&P 500 price target to 8,400 from 8,250 and lifted 2026 EPS estimates to $375, citing 'fabulous earnings momentum.' The CNN fear/greed index reached 62/100 (greed territory), and VIX briefly touched a 7-month low at 14.84. SPY shows $4.4B call open interest at the 775 strike and $4.3B at 780, indicating strong bullish positioning.

bullets.title: NBIS Q2 capacity-constrained, not demand-constrained; BE +14% on NBIS Bloom Energy switch
bullets.body: NBIS Q2 call framing: AI infrastructure market is constrained by deployable, production-ready capacity—not end demand—making capacity providers the key beneficiary. BE surged 14% intraday on reports that NBIS's call included discussion of a switch to Bloom Energy technology.

bullets.title: DELL up 77% since Trump endorsement; SMCI TP raised to $54 on strong F4Q26
bullets.body: DELL has surged approximately 77% since Trump said 'go out and buy a Dell.' Separately, one analyst raised SMCI's target price to $54 on a strong F4Q26 gross margin beat of 17.6%, FY27 revenue guidance raised to $65–$72B, a $60B backlog, and no further dilution expected. SpaceX exposure was flagged as a key upside factor.

bullets.title: UBER developing kids ride tier for ages 10+; invests in Chilean motorcycle-financing fintech
bullets.body: Uber is building a new 'tween' ride tier for children as young as 10, integrated with Uber Family profiles and background-checked drivers. Separately, Uber is investing in Chilean fintech Galgo, which specializes in extending credit for motorcycle purchases—part of its broader international expansion.

bullets.title: Scale-across optics TAM crystallizing; CIEN, ANET, CSCO, NOK, VIAV moving design wins to orders
bullets.body: Scale-across optics for AI/data center networking is moving from design wins into order books, with companies including Arista, Cisco, Ciena, Nokia, and VIAVI providing TAM guidance for high-end optics. Optical infrastructure scaling still faces 6-inch wafer manufacturing constraints at scale per a Microsoft-cited source.
